excerpt: Moov is a US payments platform for software companies: card acceptance, ACH, wallets and payouts through one API. Published pricing, funding and alternatives.
content:
Moov is a US payments infrastructure company. Software platforms use its API to accept card and bank payments from their customers, hold money in wallets and send it out again as payouts, which matters for businesses such as marketplaces, lending platforms and vertical software that move money between several parties. Its site calls it the payments platform powering choice, built for technical teams. Customers shown on its site include Jack Henry, LoanPro, Trimble, Valon, Canopy and Super Dispatch.

Moov was founded in 2018 by Wade Arnold, who earlier sold the banking technology startup Banno to Jack Henry & Associates; its roots are in open-source banking software. Fortune reported in January 2023 that Moov had raised a $45 million Series B led by Commerce Ventures, with Andreessen Horowitz, Bain Capital Ventures, Sorenson Ventures and Visa, which was investing for the first time. That brought total funding to $77.5 million, after a $5.5 million seed round in August 2020 and a $27 million Series A in December 2020. The company then had 72 employees.

Moov publishes its prices. Standard pricing is pay-as-you-go with no setup fees and a $500 monthly minimum. US card acceptance costs interchange plus 0.60% plus 15 cents per charge (0.50% plus 15 cents for Tap to Pay), international cards add 1.5%, and disputes are $15. Same-day ACH is 40 cents a transfer and next-day ACH 25 cents, with $5 per return. Monthly fees include $5 per business for a merchant processing account, $2 for PCI compliance and 50 cents per active wallet. Custom pricing is available for high volumes.

Moov suits software companies building payments into their products in the US. Small merchants who just want to take cards will find simpler options.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
